name: Your Name
current_status: One-line positioning statement — what you are, how long you have been doing it, and what you build.
summary: Two or three sentences the assistant can paraphrase when someone asks who you are. Cover the kind of systems you design, the domains you have worked in, and the through-line across your roles. Write it in the third person — the assistant speaks about you, not as you.
strengths: A capability you would be comfortable being interviewed on.
A second capability, phrased concretely rather than as a buzzword.
A third — include the scale or constraint that makes it credible.
tech_at_glance: AWS (Lambda, Step Functions, SQS, SNS, DynamoDB, API Gateway, SAM)
services: A kind of work you take on, described as an outcome rather than a job title.
A second kind of work, with the discipline or method you bring to it.
A third — name the domain where you are strongest.
engagement_targets: The kind of full-time role you want, and the ownership level you need.
The kind of consulting or contract work you would take.
Project-shaped work you are open to: an MVP, a migration, a hardening pass.
speaking_points: A story you want the assistant to be able to tell — a specific accomplishment, the constraint that made it hard, what you did, and the result. Four or five sentences, third person.
A second story, from a different role or domain, so the assistant is not repeating itself.
A third story covering a different dimension — leadership, a rescue, a decision you would defend.
A note on how you work: tooling, process, quality bar. This is where the assistant answers 'how does he approach X'.
contact_preference: The contact form on this site is the preferred channel. Every submission is read.
